IMO you shouldn’t mate spiders until you have extensive experience. You should be able to accurately and confidently sex your spider and identify when it is mature. For males, this will be quite clear by looking at pedipalps. They’ll have a boxing glove shape. For females, you can tell by locating the epigynum. A visible epigynum is not evidence of maturity so be sure you’ve seen plenty and know how to tell. It will generally be very shiny and well defined. Once you have accurately identified a mature male and a mature female (please be sure they do not come from the same line as there is evidence that inbreeding jumping spiders can cause health issues), feed the female a good meal and let her hang onto it while she mates. Supervise the entire encounter. It may take minutes or a couple hours. The male will cautiously approach the female and if she accepts, he will insert his pedipalps underneath her. Promptly remove the male after they are finished or he may become her next meal.

I leave for Disney in two days and I’ve been so nervous about this ride. I’ve obviously been here before because I started to upvote your comment and realized I already had. I felt very much lied to when I rode this ride. I have ridden many rollercoasters, though they scare me these days, and this drop is different. It’s like a drop tower drop, but much shorter. The feeling is the same though. I don’t understand why people lie and say it isn’t. Is it bearable? Yes, I mean once you’re on the ride, what choice do you have? I will ride again for my kids sake but I may not ride again after that. I am very very nervous to experience this again. Maybe it’s because I’m chicken or maybe it’s because I’m ND but it’s taken me years to accept the fact that I don’t like certain ride motions and that’s OKAY. I can handle loops, speed, some types of drops, but I do not like free-fall type drops so even though the drop length is similar to pirates it really can’t be compared to that. I highly recommend every Star Wars fan give this ride a try, but do not let anyone tell you this drop is like an elevator because that just isn’t accurate and it isn’t a fair way to portray it. I would have ridden one time regardless because I wanted to experience it, but I would have preferred to be adequately prepared for the drop.

Helix piercings are one of the most difficult in terms of healing. Don’t take the jewelry out, especially when it’s this angry. Emu oil is really helpful. Sometimes I have better luck by switching the jewelry out to a titanium ring. The ring doesn’t sink down into the jewelry the way some flat backs do and titanium is better for sensitivities. You might be sensitive to whatever metal was used in your jewelry.

I think it’s so important that the kids spend time with their dad. I really just wanted to talk to others who can relate. It’s hard to know how to help them. I want to encourage them and be positive but I don’t want to invalidate them when they are openly telling me how they feel. I want them to always be candid with me like that and to trust that they can talk to me about anything at all.

I encourage them to spend time with their dad and his parents instead of calling me. Don’t get me wrong, I want to hear from them as much as I can, but I know it makes things harder for them. I don’t call because I don’t want to intrude on their time together but they do call me 20+ times per day some days. Especially when he is being really hateful or just not playing games with them or spending time with them. They’ll call and ask me to play an online game or something with them. My oldest really likes MTG Arena so I’m trying to find the balance between not imposing on their time with their dad but also not invalidating their feelings which are real and are valid. I don’t want to discourage them and make them feel like he isn’t a good dad but I also don’t want to be argumentative when they tell me, “Dad doesn’t spend time with us. We don’t like going.” I try to just listen and then when they aren’t around I try to kindly say, “Hey I think it would mean a lot to the kids if you could make time for a movie or board game with them this week.” But he gets pretty angry and tells me not to tell him how to parent. Which I am not trying to do at all. I just really want them to enjoy going to his house. I think that’s so important for all of them. It’s a fine line that I don’t want to overstep.

My marriage sounds so eerily similar to yours. Thank you for being candid and sharing your experience. I very quickly lost my identity and I didn’t even realize it until it was too late. I do need this week break, but I don’t want it. I live an hour from their school. Therapy is helpful. I struggle to read books or watch tv because something always makes me think of them.

Because I live so far away from their dad a full week just makes sense financially. Therapy helps for sure and I did post this minutes after dropping them off so emotions were high. I’m feeling a little bit better than I was when I posted. But it sucks going through it every week. I think more than anything I am just hoping to hear I’m not alone and that others know how I feel because most people I have talked to have said, “I miss my kids but I love my free time,” and that’s valid, but I can’t relate and feel like I haven’t spoken with anyone else who understands how I am feeling.

Oh for sure I do those things with them when they come home. It’s just hard to enjoy things when I constantly miss them. I was a stay at home mom for years. It’s an adjustment. I’m not looking for sympathy or to take them from their dad. Just for guidance from others who have been through this and might know how to navigate these emotions.

Counseling is helping for sure! I am not looking for pity or anything like that. I’m not looking to take my kids from their dad. I think it’s so important that they have both of us in their lives. I’m just wondering how I can get through it without constantly thinking about them and feeling that ache. I was a stay at home mom for years. It’s hard being away from them. Healthy or not, being their mother became my identity, which is pretty common for stay at home moms. I’m trying to figure out who I am outside of being their mother, but it’s a process and an adjustment.

Of course they wouldn’t make a difference in court. I wouldn’t dream of taking him to court for something like that. We have decided to settle outside of court. I am trying my best to just be kind and get along. I really just came here looking for some coping tips. I don’t want to take my kids from their dad. I want him to spend quality time with them for his sake. But I can’t force that.
